To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified six CEBM design options that companies can use to close material flows in the CE and we discussed different design strategies to implement them.

the circular economy requires a new approach for companies to create value and that this approach is reflected in a variety of business model design strategies that can be classified into six CEBM patterns.

the current literature proposes six major circular economy business model patterns, namely, repair and maintenance; refurbishment and recycling; cascading; organic feedstock; reuse and redistribution and remanufacture, that are based on the reuse and/or recovery of resources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing a systematic overview of CEBMs, which can help companies to develop and design CEBMs that are appropriate for their context.
the identification of CEBMs and the development of a typology of CEBM patterns.
the development of a typology of CEBMs, which can help practitioners in the development of CEBMs and academics in the development of future research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no universal CEBM design principles.
the circular economy business model literature provides a broad range of CEBM patterns and design options, which are currently underexplored.
there are six major circular economy business model patterns, each of which can be implemented in different ways, and each of which can have a positive impact on the environment and society.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current literature on CEBM design is still in its infancy, but it is growing and maturing.
we have identified six business model patterns for circular economy business model design and have discussed the design strategies for each.

there is a wide range of CEBMs that can be designed to support the transition to the CE, and that these can be grouped into a limited set of patterns that can serve as a starting point for further research on CEBMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CEBM patterns identified in this paper can serve as a reference for practitioners and researchers to design new CEBMs and assess the potential of their existing CEBMs.
the CEBM patterns can be applied to any product or service, and they are applicable in different industries, thus offering a useful framework to guide the development of circular business models.
CEBMs can be classified into a set of major design patterns.
